I am 70 this year, and I have been farming these 10.1 mu for 15 years since my husband stopped working the fields. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and keep my own accounts. My son works in a factory in Handan, but he comes back for busy seasons. My daughter-in-law and grandchildren also help when school is out. We have seven people in the house, and some wages come from outside, but the land is still our root.

I split my 10.1 mu into two parts. Seven mu I do wheat and maize rotation — that is my bread and butter. The other 3.1 mu I plant cotton for cash. We have a well, so water is not my biggest worry, but electricity for the pump costs money.

I always start from what I did last year. Last year my wheat got about 900 jin per mu, maize got about 1,100 jin per mu, and cotton gave me around 400 jin of seed cotton per mu. These numbers are acceptable. I will not change my methods drastically because at my age, a failed crop is a disaster.

For the 7 mu of winter wheat: last autumn I already rotary-tilled and sowed improved Jinmai variety wheat at about 15 jin of seed per mu. I put down 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer — the bag says 15-15-15 — as base fertilizer. This spring, when the wheat turns green, I will topdress with 25 kg per mu of urea. The input dealer tells me to use slow-release fertilizer, but my neighbor Old Wang tried it last year and spent more money for the same yield. No thanks. My wheat gets four irrigations: winter water, reviving water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. I spray pesticide twice — once for weeds and once for insects at heading. I expect about 920 jin per mu this year, around 460 kg.

For the 7 mu of summer maize: after wheat harvest in June, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed directly into the wheat stubble. No-tillage saves time and the stubble keeps moisture. I use 5 jin of seed per mu. I put 40 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound as base fertilizer, and at the big trumpet stage I topdress with 20 kg per mu of urea. I irrigate three times — seedling, jointing, and filling. Two sprays: herbicide after emergence, and one insecticide if I see corn borer. Expected yield is about 1,140 jin per mu, say 570 kg.

For the 3.1 mu of cotton: I plough this field deep in spring because cotton roots need soft soil. I plant improved Bt cotton, about 3 jin of seed per mu. Base fertilizer is 40 kg per mu of compound 15-15-15. I topdress twice: at flowering with 15 kg urea, and at bolling with 10 kg potassium sulfate. Cotton pests are terrible, so I spray five times this year — aphids, spider mites, and bollworm all need watching. I irrigate three times. Last year I got 400 jin seed cotton per mu; this year I hope for the same, about 200 kg.

I calculate my costs carefully. A 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer is about 160 yuan now, and urea is about 120 yuan. For all my land, fertilizer is my biggest expense after seeds. But I dare not cut back — if I use too little and yields drop, I lose more money than I save. I would rather put a little extra than risk a bad harvest. I watch what my neighbors do. Auntie Li on the east side uses almost the same amounts as me, and her yields are stable, so I sleep well at night. My budget is tight but with off-farm income we manage. I will not hire outside labor except maybe for cotton picking if the family cannot all come back.
